### [Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth](https://deepmind.google/blog/introducing-alphaproof-code/)

**Google DeepMind** · 2026-11-10

Google DeepMind has introduced AlphaProof Code, an agent system that generated three million lines of Lean proofs to verify the core encryption of the Signal protocol.

- The target verification language used by the agents was Lean.
- The system successfully verified the core encryption implementation of the Signal messaging protocol.

**Why it matters:** Demonstrates the capability of automated proof agents to formally verify large-scale, critical real-world cryptographic codebases.

### [Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/10/muse-ember/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-11-10

Meta AI has launched Muse Ember 1.0, a highly efficient reasoning model targeting agentic tasks like coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and tool calls across a 1-million-token context window.

- Base pricing starts at $0.10/M input ($0.004/M cached) and $0.50/M output for prompts under 200k tokens, scaling to $0.30/M input and $1.50/M output above 200k tokens.
- Positioned directly on the Artificial Analysis Pareto efficiency frontier, offering competitive cost-per-task metrics relative to GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5.
- Features six distinct reasoning levels: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max.
- Delivers SVG generation quality comparable to the 40x more expensive Muse Wonder model.

**Why it matters:** Muse Ember establishes a new cost-to-performance benchmark on the Pareto frontier for high-volume, repetitive developer agent tasks and long-document processing.

`ai` `meta` `llm-pricing` `llm-release` `generative-ai`

### [llm-anthropic 0.31](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/9/llm-anthropic/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-11-09

Version 0.31 of the llm-anthropic plugin adds support for Anthropic's newly released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models.

- Fable 5.2 is priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, reflecting a 20% price reduction from Fable 5.1.
- The model introduces a bug at the 'max' reasoning effort level where it depletes its 128,000 token budget on thinking without returning an output, matching behavior seen in Opus 5.5.
- Reasoning levels low, medium, high, and xhigh executed successfully via the CLI using the model identifier claude-fable-5.2.
- Anthropic claims Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in black hole physics and achieved a first-place ranking on Artificial Analysis.

**Why it matters:** Developers using the llm CLI tool can now access Anthropic's flagship Fable 5.2 model at lower token rates, though they must avoid the 'max' reasoning level setting to prevent token exhaustion failures.

### [Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/10/prompting-claude-fable-52/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-11-10

Anthropic documentation for Claude Fable 5.2 reveals that explicitly assigning codebase ownership to the model significantly increases its tendency to refactor and consolidate repeated code.

- Without explicit ownership prompts, Claude Fable 5.2 defaults to adding onto existing code structures, often duplicating code.
- Including the prompt text 'This codebase is yours: what it's for and how it's built are your call, and you'll keep building on it' alters model behavior.
- In Anthropic's testing on small coding tasks, the ownership prompt increased repeated code merging from under 10% of attempts to approximately 50% of attempts.

**Why it matters:** Framing codebase ownership in prompts provides a direct lever for controlling whether the model conservatively appends code or actively refactors existing architectural debt.

`prompt-engineering` `anthropic` `claude` `llms` `code-generation`
